issues.title: Paid sick leave and expired COVID-19 quarantine leave
issues.summary: Current explanations of ordinary paid sick leave and the separate COVID quarantine-leave sunset.
issues.scope: New York State agency guidance relevant to private-sector paid sick leave; selected NYC point only where the Attorney General discusses it.
legal_questions: What leave must private employers provide under Labor Law 196-b, including amount, accrual, use, documentation, carryover, and paid prenatal leave?
Do currently accessible New York State agency pages accurately explain whether the separate COVID-19 quarantine leave enacted in 2020 remains available after its July 31, 2025 statutory sunset?
Where a state agency describes New York City sick leave, is that description consistent with the city's binding rule?
issues.status: Initial finding approved after independent and 30 October source checks
issues.limitations: The lead agency page and governing sources were recaptured on 30 October 2026. Remaining documents are only partially screened. The 2022 FAQ is still linked but visibly older. The 68-page P737 compendium has not been fully reviewed. No actual worker harm was found.

issues.title: New York unemployment insurance hearing and appeal deadlines
issues.summary: Hearing-request and appeal deadlines in current unemployment insurance guidance.
issues.scope: Bounded initial issue sweep of current NYSDOL public pages on claimant hearing requests, appeal deadlines, and selected benefit guidance. This is a targeted claim screen, not a full-document screen or exhaustive audit.
legal_questions: For a claimant disputing an initial unemployment insurance determination, does a mailed hearing request have to reach NYSDOL within 30 days, or does a timely postmark suffice?
What is the deadline for an appeal from an administrative law judge to the Unemployment Insurance Appeal Board?
Do currently displayed benefit summaries use day-of-work eligibility language that may misstate current partial-benefit rules?
issues.status: Initial finding approved after independent and 30 October source checks
issues.limitations: Only selected page sections and claims have been checked. The Appeal Board still posts the rule and applied its receipt calculation in a May 2026 decision; its latest official printed NYCRR supplement was not available for direct inspection. No actual lost appeal was found.

rules.text: For covered private employees, provides the size/income tiers, at least one hour accrued per 30 hours worked, enumerated sick/safe uses, 20 hours separate paid prenatal leave from January 1, 2025, limits on verification/disclosure, carryover with annual use caps, protection against retaliation, and records on request. The ordinary sick-leave entitlement remains in force after the separate COVID quarantine statute expired.
rules.exact_text: Every employer shall be required to provide its employees with sick leave as follows:
rules.effective_date: Ordinary sick-leave accrual began 2020-09-30 and use began 2021-01-01; paid prenatal provision effective 2025-01-01.
rules.applicability: Employee works in New York for a private employer. Unpaid versus paid leave depends on employer headcount and previous-tax-year net income. Existing equivalent policies and qualifying collective bargaining agreements may satisfy or vary § 196-b requirements; NYC may enforce stronger local rules.
rules.qualifications: Employee works in New York for a private employer. Unpaid versus paid leave depends on employer headcount and previous-tax-year net income. Existing equivalent policies and qualifying collective bargaining agreements may satisfy or vary § 196-b requirements; NYC may enforce stronger local rules.

rules.citation: L. 2024, ch. 56, Part M, § 1 (amending L. 2020, ch. 25, § 2)
rules.text: The special 2020 COVID-19 mandatory/precautionary quarantine or isolation leave law was made to expire and be deemed repealed July 31, 2025. The Senate's A8806C page records the final bill as signed chapter 56 on April 20, 2024; final Part M appears at page text lines 14862-14872.
rules.exact_text: shall expire and be deemed repealed July 31, 2025
rules.applicability: Addresses only the special COVID quarantine/isolation leave and associated benefits under the 2020 act. It does not repeal ordinary sick leave under Labor Law § 196-b, other existing protections, or necessarily resolve claims that arose before sunset.
rules.qualifications: Addresses only the special COVID quarantine/isolation leave and associated benefits under the 2020 act. It does not repeal ordinary sick leave under Labor Law § 196-b, other existing protections, or necessarily resolve claims that arose before sunset.

rules.text: Ordinary sick-leave verification may not be required for an absence shorter than three consecutive previously scheduled workdays/shifts. At three or more such days, permitted documentation is narrowly limited; no confidential reason or employee-paid verification costs.
rules.applicability: NYC's local law has a distinct, more protective threshold for its own protected time-off entitlement.
rules.qualifications: NYC's local law has a distinct, more protective threshold for its own protected time-off entitlement.

rules.text: For NYC protected time off, the employer may require reasonable documentation only after more than three consecutive workdays, subject to policy and reimbursement requirements. This is distinct from the state regulation's three-or-more scheduled-day threshold.
rules.applicability: Only NYC covered employment; included because the NY Attorney General expressly discusses NYC.
rules.qualifications: Only NYC covered employment; included because the NY Attorney General expressly discusses NYC.

rules.text: A claimant dissatisfied with an initial determination may request a hearing within thirty days after mailing or personal delivery of notice. A referee may extend the period where physical condition or mental incapacity prevented the claimant from filing within thirty days.
rules.exact_text: within thirty days after the mailing or personal delivery of notice of such determination, request a hearing
rules.effective_date: Current statutory text rechecked 2026-10-30; latest revision date shown by NY Senate: 2014-09-22.
rules.qualifications: Check party, notice, filing method, and any statutory exception.

rules.text: A hearing request is timely if postmarked within 30 days of the party's receipt of the determination, or if there is specified other proof of submission, including electronic submission, fax acknowledgment, certified mailing receipt, stamped receipt, or neutral-party proof of personal service. Absent contrary proof, determination is deemed mailed on date stated and received no later than five business days later.

claims.exact_quote: NYS COVID-19 Leave benefits and protections are still in effect and have no expiration date.
claims.location: body paragraph below title, source text line 60
claims.surrounding_context: The surrounding DOL paragraph discusses mandatory or precautionary COVID quarantine/isolation orders and links special COVID Paid Sick Leave fact sheets.
claims.analysis: A currently presented no-expiration claim directly conflicts with the enacted July 31, 2025 expiration of the special 2020 COVID quarantine leave. The ordinary §196-b sick-leave entitlement still exists, but it is a different benefit.
claims.counterargument: The DOL could mean general sick leave for COVID illness under §196-b; however its specific reference to quarantine/isolation orders, extra protections, and linked special COVID fact sheets points to the repealed 2020 program.
claims.reviewer_outcome: Independent reviewer verified the DOL sentence, signed sunset, WCB confirmation, and surviving ordinary sick leave. The source set was recaptured on 30 October 2026 before initial publication.
claims.example: A covered worker receives a new COVID isolation order in October 2026 after using available ordinary sick leave, and expects extra quarantine leave under the 2020 act. That special statutory entitlement expired in July 2025; other leave depends on separate facts.
claims.potential_consequence: A worker may plan around extra quarantine leave that the 2020 act no longer provides, potentially delaying a request for other available leave or benefits. No reliance has been documented.
claims.limitations: DOL's original posting date is unknown. The current source and law were recaptured on 30 October 2026. No actual worker reliance or loss is documented. Other protections are not categorically assessed.

claims.exact_quote: Your written request must be received within 30 days of the determination.
claims.surrounding_context: The Contact page places this categorical statement directly above an address for mailing a hearing request; it does not describe the postmark or receipt presumption there.
claims.analysis: On an ordinary mailed request, 'received' requires agency receipt by day 30, whereas the Appeal Board rule expressly treats a request postmarked within 30 days of the party's receipt of the determination as timely. The public wording can make a claimant believe a timely mailed request is already too late.
claims.counterargument: The contact page may intend a cautious filing recommendation; other DOL pages accurately explain postmark. Yet the wording uses 'must' and 'received' under a mailing address, so it states a mandatory condition broader than the rule.
claims.reviewer_outcome: Independent reviewer confirmed the restrictive DOL wording, Appeal Board postmark/receipt rule, current DOL FAQ, and May 2026 Board application. The claim, rule PDF, statute, and decision were recaptured on 30 October 2026. No conflicting later rule was located; the latest official printed supplement was not directly inspected.
claims.example: A determination is received five business days after mailing. A claimant posts a signed hearing request 29 calendar days after receipt; DOL receives it four days later. The cited rule treats the postmark as timely, subject to contrary receipt proof and filing qualifications.
claims.potential_consequence: A person might forgo a hearing request or rush an unnecessary alternative submission based on an inaccurate perceived deadline. No real-world instance or loss established.
claims.limitations: The Appeal Board's posted rule PDF carries a 2020 internal revision date. The Board applied the receipt calculation in May 2026, but the latest official printed supplement was not available for direct inspection. No notice exemplar or actual lost appeal is documented.
